newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks pare gains on Lozano firing, end up.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks pare gains on Lozano firing, end up.

text.p: Mexican stocks closed off their highs on Monday, falling slightly near the close of trade on news that Mexican Attorney General Antonio Lozano was fired, traders said.

The IPC index of blue-chip stocks closed 19.38 points or 0.59 percent higher at 3,311.07 points, losing about 15 points immediately following the announcement, but gaining back about five points in the final minute of trade.
"It's crazy here," on trader said as the news broke. "People are putting in all kinds of sell orders out there."
Volume was weak at 77.96 million shares traded.
On the broad market, 103 stocks changed hands, of which winners beat losers by 50 to 34. Blue chips were largely absent from the day's trading activity.
For most of the session, traders said stocks gained on local and foreign bargain hunters stepping in and expectations primary rates would fall.
Nonetheless, the Lozano news abruptly changed what had been a modestly optimistic market, they added.
"The news of changeover in the Attorney General's office definitely hit the market," said Roberto Solano, an analyst at the Estrategia Bursatil brokerage.
"The political background has held the bourse back, because economic fundamentals and technicals do favor a rally," he said.
"We were happy and then they went and changed the game on us. Dealers with discretion to buy and trade on their own behalf were most scared," said a floor trader.
"The news is not good and we'll have to wait and see if it is interpreted as a party political move ahead of (mid-term) elections in 1997," he added.
Lozano, of the National Action Party, was the first member of an opposition party to be named to a cabinet post in decades.
